subject: VALUE clause
notes: kb/Work PB502 (landed) - GR18 defers wholly to 14.7.8, and every sentence of 14.7.8 is now realized for the condition-name VALUE range. Rule 1 (numeric range = literal-1, literal-2 and all algebraic values between) CONFORMED throughout. Rule 2's no-phrase arm (the implementor default, which for this compiler is the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE) and its inverted-range EC-RANGE-INVALID sentence CONFORMED throughout. THE `IN alphabet-name-1` PARAGRAPH, which was a silent wrong answer, was cured by the PB398 landing (2573338e): DataBinder.BindCondition resolves the phrase through the ONE resolver DataBinder.Switches#TryResolveRangeAlphabet that EVALUATE's range-expression also takes - 14.7.8 opens 'this specification applies to THROUGH phrases specified in the VALUE clause and the EVALUATE statement', so one sentence governs both clauses and one resolver answers them - Condition88.Alphabet carries the name, and ConditionRenderer#RangeCollateArg hands that alphabet's carrier to the range test in place of ctx.CollateArg. RE-MEASURED on a freshly built cobol.exe, 2026-09-13, at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023, identical on all four: under `ALPHABET ALPHA-REV IS "Z" THRU "A"` (12.3.7.4 GR7 k) 5., so Z=1 ... A=26, P=11, M=14, D=23) and `01 WS-A PIC X VALUE "M"`, `88 A-RNG VALUE "P" THRU "D" IN ALPHA-REV` is TRUE (11 <= 14 <= 23) and `VALUE "D" THRU "P" IN ALPHA-REV` is FALSE (23 > 11, inverted, empty) - the two answers the adjudication recorded WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, both right now, and each the OPPOSITE of its native-sequence answer. THE INVERSION TEST ITSELF RUNS ON THE NAMED SEQUENCE, not the native one: under `>>TURN EC-RANGE-INVALID CHECKING ON` the alphabet-inverted range sets EC-RANGE-INVALID while the alphabet-ascending one (which is inverted NATIVELY) sets nothing. 14.7.8 rule 2's LOCALE sentence also holds - `ALPHABET LOC IS LOCALE` with `88 C-LOC VALUE "a" THRU "z" IN LOC` answers TRUE for "A", the locale ordering's answer and the opposite of the native one, on the VALUE-clause AND EVALUATE arms alike. THE UNDER-REJECTION HALF IS CLOSED: an undeclared alphabet-name is COBOL1997, a numeric THROUGH range carrying the phrase is COBOL1998 (SR31 sentence 1) and a class mismatch either way is COBOL1999 (SR31 sentence 2). The national THROUGH range that used to be staged loud at COBOL0899 now runs (kb/Work PB761). WITNESSES: the 2002 positive golden names NO PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, so rule 2's no-phrase arm resolves to the native order and every leg is the opposite of its no-phrase twin - dropping the phrase again flips a line. That is deliberately unlike the sibling golden 2002/pb398_range_in_alphabet, which makes the named alphabet the PCS and whose level-88 legs therefore answer the same either way.
